summary.en: Devised boats and carts, ranged across the realm, mapped land and divided provinces into myriad hundred-li states.
summary.zh: 作舟車以濟不通，旁行天下，畫野分州，得百里之國萬區

summary.en: Faced the great flood that split the realm; established twelve provinces and ordered Yu to control the waters.
summary.zh: 堯遭洪水，天下分絕，為十二州，使禹治之

summary.en: Ordered Yu to regulate the floodwaters.
After waters and lands were leveled, recast the realm as nine provinces, set five service zones, and assigned tribute by local produce.
summary.zh: 水土既平，更制九州，列五服，任土作貢

summary.en: Ordered by Yao to bring the floodwaters under control.
Spread out the land, cut mountain paths, and fixed high mountains and great rivers (Yugong survey).
summary.zh: 禹敷土，隨山刊木，奠高山大川

summary.en: Opening of the Yugong geographic survey attributed to Yu.

claims.event: Reign of Emperor Wu of Han; chapter cites his frontier campaigns and provincial reorganization without a single regnal year.

summary.en: Received the abdication from Shun and founded the house of Xia.
Directed the channeling of Weakwater, Blackwater, Yellow River, Han, Yangtze, Ji, Huai, Wei, and Luo as described in the Yugong hydrography.
Received the dark jade tablet and announced successful completion of the works.
Granted lands and surnames with the injunction to put virtue first.
summary.zh: 錫土姓：「祗台德先，不距朕行。」

summary.en: Declared: Reverently put virtue first; do not oppose what I intend to do.
Later Zhou-era geography notes that descendant marquises from Taihao still survived.
Later Zhou-era geography notes that descendant lines from the Yellow Emperor still survived.
Tang (Yao) marquises were said still to survive in later records.
Yu (Shun) marquises were said still to survive in later records.
Drove back the Hu and Yue, opened new frontiers, established Jiaozhi in the south and Shuofang in the north, and set up thirteen inspectorates.
summary.zh: 武帝攘卻胡、越，開地斥境，南置交阯，北置朔方之州…凡十三部，置刺史

translationRepairs: Bamboo and reeds spread; scrub and tall trees rose.
Bamboo and reeds spread; grasses flourished and trees grew tall.
The received text's 魇 is a transcription corruption in the standard Yu Gong phrase 草夭木喬; the repair restores its sense of luxuriant grasses and tall trees.
Bamboo and reeds spread; scrub and tall trees rose.
Bamboo and reeds had spread; grasses flourished and trees were tall.
The literal field needs the same restored Yu Gong reading, but 夭 here means flourishing rather than merely young or vigorous.
From Min and Qi they went on to Jing Mountain and crossed the Yellow River;
From Qian and Qi they went on to Jing Mountain and crossed the Yellow River;
The Yu Gong route is 導岍及岐; Qian is required, whereas Min would correspond to 岷.
Following Min and Qi, they reached Jing Mountain and crossed the River;
Following Qian and Qi, they reached Jing Mountain and crossed the River;
The literal field has the same Qian/Min reading error as the idiomatic field.
Five hundred li of Yao service: three hundred li Yi, two hundred li Cai.
Five hundred li of the constrained service zone: three hundred li of the Yi zone, two hundred li of the Cai zone.
要服 is a Five Domains category, not Emperor Yao; 'constrained service zone' gives its function without pretending it is a personal name or an ethnographic gloss.
Five hundred li of Yao service: three hundred li Yi, two hundred li Cai.
Five hundred li of constrained service: three hundred li of Yi, two hundred li of Cai.
要服 is a service-zone label, not the personal name Yao; the literal rendering should therefore not capitalize it as a name.
